clue.text: He was a French painter till our revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns everything over, so the letters of the two words that follow are reordered

explanation.surface: A remark that a French artist was once part of our own revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' rearranges TILLOUR into the painter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Utrillo was a French artist famous for his Montmartre street scenes.

clue.text: Don't put on enough-vest and pants only

explanation.surface: Someone underdressed, wearing nothing but a vest and pants.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: to 'under-wear' would be to wear too little.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn too sparingly reads as wearing under the mark; vests and pants are the garments beneath outer clothes.

clue.text: On in time for an award

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Arriving punctually to collect a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: An honour is a distinction or decoration conferred on someone, such as a knighthood.

clue.text: Knack that can be acquired without difficulty?

definitions.text: Knack that can be acquired without difficulty?

parts.words: Knack that can be acquired without difficulty?
parts.note: a skill that comes easily; the word for such an aptitude also means ease itself

explanation.surface: A musing on talents that come easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Facility means both an aptitude for something and the ease with which it is done.

clue.text: Amazingly bride first found these to be seemingly sweeter than others

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a plural noun: things that seem more delightful

indicators.note: something done amazingly is done in a startling way, so the letters of the next three words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A bride, to her amazement, discovers that certain pleasures taste better than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazingly' scrambles BRIDEFIRSTFOUND; 'these to be' links the fodder to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially, stolen pleasures taste sweetest, which is why prohibited delights seem more appealing.

clue.text: Do not agree with war

explanation.surface: Disagreeing with the idea of fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to clash or be at odds; as a noun it means armed fighting between nations.

clue.text: Very easy to carry

parts.note: describes something weighing little, which is also a word for undemanding

explanation.surface: A description of a handy, portable load.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of little weight is simple to lift and transport.

clue.text: Tribal leader in another ritual existing in name only

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Tribal
another version of the word ritual means its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A tribal chief taking part in yet another ceremony, though only nominally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes T from Tribal; 'another' reshuffles RITUAL to ITULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A titular head holds a title or position without real power.

clue.text: Smart circle's strong tipple

parts.note: to smart is to sting with pain
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A clever social set enjoying a powerful drink.
explanation.walkthrough: STINGO is an old name for strong beer or ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingo is an old term for a potent ale.

clue.text: Vagabond to enter an opening in the wall

parts.note: to run in a race or for office is to enter it
the indefinite article gives A
a gate is a way through a wall

explanation.surface: A tramp trying to get in through a gap in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Runagate is an archaic word for a wanderer or fugitive.

clue.text: Minute weapon?

parts.note: minute looks like tiny but means a unit of time: a weapon timed to go off

explanation.surface: A question about a tiny armament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' wants to be read as tiny; read it as sixty seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosive device set to detonate at a set moment is governed by the clock.

clue.text: Not much by itself in degrees

explanation.surface: A small amount, taken gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little by little' means by degrees, so the word 'by itself' (placed beside its own copy with 'by') gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Small means a small amount; the phrase repeating it with 'by' means gradually.

clue.text: Belonging to earlier times in the Eastern hemisphere

explanation.surface: Something old-fashioned found in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: It describes quaint old-fashioned charm, and also names Europe, Asia and Africa as known before the Americas.

clue.text: Cut short by a few feet at the port

parts.note: to dock a tail is to cut it short
a yard is three feet

explanation.surface: Something trimmed by a few feet at the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A dockyard is a shipbuilding and repair area at a port.

clue.text: Sailor, possibly Cathy's husband

indicators.note: possibly signals another arrangement of the letters of the name

parts.note: the possessive letters are used as fodder
man can mean husband, as in man and wife

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Cathy's husband is a mariner.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sails a yacht is a type of seafarer.

clue.text: Imagined rude miss running amok

indicators.note: letters running amok are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Picturing an ill-mannered young woman running wild.
explanation.definitionFit: To surmise is to guess or suppose without proof.

clue.text: Upset by bowling spin?

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
a spin is a turn

explanation.surface: Disappointed by a spinning delivery in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is a set of six deliveries in cricket, the British bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn is to upset or knock over, or to reverse a decision.

clue.text: Break law, mixing oil in tank with energy!

indicators.note: in puts the mixed letters within the container

parts.note: a vat is a large tank

indicators.note: mixing the word oil scrambles its letters

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Breaking a rule by blending oil in a tank with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark and 'tank' suggest a military vehicle, but the tank here is a large vessel for liquids, with the scrambled oil sitting inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate is to infringe or breach a rule.

clue.text: No sense disturbing unity

indicators.note: disturbing the letters of these two words jumbles them

explanation.surface: Senselessness unsettling harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Oneness is the state of being whole and united.

clue.text: Charming fellow gets the print

parts.note: an etching is a print made from an etched plate

explanation.surface: An attractive man receives the print.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching means attractive or appealing.

clue.text: Beat the interminable spots

indicators.note: interminable means without end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: Fighting endless spots on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash is to beat soundly.

clue.text: Two washers put back on the weapon

indicators.note: put back means the run of letters is written in reverse
two calls for the same word twice

parts.note: a mop is used for washing floors

explanation.surface: Replacing a pair of washers on a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A pom-pom is a rapid-firing anti-aircraft cannon.

clue.text: One setting the speed has to step to one side

parts.note: a pace is a step
R for right is one side

explanation.surface: A pacemaker stepping aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacer is a runner who sets the tempo for others.

clue.text: We hear you purchasing a rebellion

indicators.note: we hear tells us the clue words sound like the entry

parts.note: prising means getting purchase or leverage, so the phrase sounds like 'you prising'

explanation.surface: Someone notes your purchase is a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: Purchase means leverage, so 'purchasing' is prising.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a revolt against authority.

clue.text: Large number included in variety of raisins-or flowers

indicators.note: included in places a letter within the mixed letters
a variety of raisins is a different arrangement of the word

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred appearing in a mix of dried fruit or blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Daffodils are a type of bulb plant of this genus.

clue.text: Sower initially cultivated pears that were thinly scattered

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Sower
cultivated soil is worked over, so the fruit word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A grower planting pears widely apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives S; 'cultivated' turns PEARS into PARSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means scanty and widely spaced.

clue.text: Man takes more than one partner to the islands

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
brides are wedding partners, plural

explanation.surface: A bigamist taking his wives to an island group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hebrides are islands off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: These are a Scottish archipelago in the Atlantic.
